items.title: 68002_Benny Waters oral history interview
items.q: See, I worked with Hot Lips Page many, many, many different times.

ctx.x: And Lips Page, when did you leave Lips Page?

Well see, I worked with Lips Page several times, you know. The first time I worked with Lips Page was down in Clinton with a small combination. The next time I worked with Lips Page is, was - I worked with Lips Page at Small's Paradise, too. Then I worked with Lips Page at the Savoy Ballroom, I worked with Hot Lips Page at Kelly's Stable. See, I worked with Hot Lips Page many, many, many different times. I worked at Small's Paradise with Hot Lips Page also and made arrangements for him.
Hey, we're gettin' a lit bit away from Boston, I think we should try to clear - why don't you tell the story, soup to nuts, of you and Harry Carney in Boston in the early '20's?

items.title: Benny Waters interviewed by Michael Woods, Los Angeles, California, September 1, 1995
items.q: Starting in 1933, Benny played for ten years in the bands of Fletcher Henderson, Jimmie Lunceford and Hot Lips Page.

ctx.x: Benny Waters lays claim to be the oldest working jazzman in the country, probably in the world. Born in Maryland in 1902, Benny showed an early musical aptitude, giving piano recitals by age seven, and soon after learning the reed instruments from his older brother. He played in dance bands while still in high school and attended the Boston Conservatory of Music where he studied piano and theory while teaching clarinet.
